field.name: execution_status
field.desc: FIRST line, followed by a one-line explanation. A verdict, not a ran/did-not-run flag; there is deliberately no SUCCESS value (see 11-execution-verdict-plan.md).

banner.name: active_namespace
banner.desc: 'active_namespace: ns-XXXX' + note, below the verdict; a '[reminder] your namespace ...' line is appended near the end too

section.name: stderr
section.desc: cleaned traceback/warnings, ANSI stripped; placed ABOVE stdout because it carries the reason for the verdict

section.name: last expression
section.desc: repr of last expression; shown ONLY when stdout is empty

section.name: artifacts
section.desc: Markdown links to new/changed ./workspace files; images as ![](), else []()

field.name: next_action
field.desc: LAST line: the single instruction the model is told to obey for this verdict

namespaceParam.desc: Mandatory on execution tools. Per-conversation isolation; see 09-namespace-routing.md.
namespaceParam.rule: Pass 'new' (or empty) on the first call to mint a fresh ns-XXXX.
Reuse the exact active_namespace value returned, on every later call.
id source priority: MCP _meta conversation id (future) > this arg > minted.

injected.name: ctx
injected.desc: FastMCP-injected, hidden from schema; carries future _meta hook

tool.name: execute_python_code
tool.description: Run Python in the namespace's stateful IPython kernel. Variables/imports persist across calls within that namespace.

input.param: Python source to execute. Use print() to return values; save plots to ./workspace.

tool.name: run_python_file
tool.description: Run an existing .py file from ./workspace as a script: its compiled source is exec'd in the kernel namespace with __file__ and sys.argv[0] set, so its __main__ block runs. Top-level names land in the kernel namespace as they are bound and survive sys.exit() or a crash. sys.exit(0) is a normal ending; a non-zero code is FAILED.

input.param: Path to a .py file INSIDE ./workspace. Accepts bare name, ./workspace/ prefix, or absolute path within the workspace.

isolation.error: execution_status: FAILED, message contains "outside the workspace"
execution_status: FAILED, message contains "is not a .py file"; checked before the kernel is touched

tool.name: write_workspace_file
tool.description: Write text content verbatim to a file inside ./workspace. Exists so a model never has to generate Python that quotes its own source in order to save a file -- the self-referential nesting that most reliably breaks small/mid-size models. Takes NO namespace: it holds no state and the workspace is shared.

input.param: Path relative to ./workspace, e.g. "fib.py" or "reports/out.md". A leading "./workspace/", "workspace/" or "/workspace/" is stripped.
Exact text to write. UTF-8, no BOM, newline="\n" so Windows text mode does not turn LF into CRLF.
Replace an existing file instead of refusing.

section.name: artifacts
section.desc: same Markdown links as the execution tools (snapshot/diff); empty diff is reported as a silent-failure warning

section.name: next
section.desc: for a .py target, a run_python_file(...) hint that also re-surfaces the namespace requirement

isolation.rule: Resolved via _resolve_new_workspace_path(); the target need not exist, so containment is checked on the PARENT after resolve().
Subdirectories are created only after the containment check passes.
isolation.error: write_status: ERROR, "pass a path relative to ./workspace"
write_status: ERROR, "reserved device name" -- Windows would otherwise accept the write and discard it
write_status: ERROR, "already exists"; message states the fix (overwrite=true or a new filename)

limit.note: 0 disables; no append mode by design

tool.name: list_workspace_files
tool.description: List every file under ./workspace with size and extension, or a note if empty.

tool.name: install_python_packages
tool.description: Install distributions from the company's intranet PyPI mirror into a side venv, so later execute_python_code calls can import them. INSTALLED means the KERNEL confirmed each distribution via importlib.metadata -- not merely that pip exited 0.

input.param: One free-form string: distribution names separated by spaces or commas, each optionally with a version specifier ("polars, rapidfuzz>=3.0"). A single string, not a list, because small models produce it far more reliably than a JSON array.

field.name: install_status
field.desc: FIRST line, followed by a one-line explanation. RUNNING is NOT a failure: the install outlived SANDBOX_TOOL_BUDGET and continues on a background thread; the response names the exact packages string to resend, and the repeat call joins the same job instead of starting a second pip.

section.name: packages
section.desc: each distribution with the version the kernel reports; '(already available)' when it was there before

section.name: why it failed
section.desc: on FAILED: one sentence naming what the USER has to fix

section.name: pip output
section.desc: on FAILED: tail of pip's own output

section.name: pip
section.desc: effective index URL and where it came from, venv path, elapsed time, pip exit code

field.name: next_action
field.desc: LAST line; on failure it says NOT to repeat the install

installTarget.rule: config.VENV_DIR, a venv created from KERNEL_PYTHON with --system-site-packages. The bundled portable Python is never modified.
Never inside ./workspace: the artifact interceptor diffs that tree and would report every installed file as a new artifact.
After a successful install the venv site-packages is added to EVERY live kernel via site.addsitedir -- no restart, so other conversations keep their loaded data.
addsitedir appends, so a package that also exists in the base install keeps winning: this tool adds packages, it does not upgrade the curated stack.

isolation.rule: Only PEP 508 requirement specifiers are accepted; the model chooses packages, the server chooses every other pip argument.

error.condition: URL, file path, editable install or pip flag

isolation.error: install_status: FAILED before pip runs, message names the rejected token

failureDiagnosis.note: With SANDBOX_PIP_RETRIES=0 pip prints NOTHING about an unreachable index, so its text alone cannot tell these apart. diagnose() probes the index instead.
failureDiagnosis.case: probe_index() fails -> names SANDBOX_PIP_INDEX_URL; if the effective index is the public PyPI, says outright that no mirror is configured on this machine

case.condition: plain-http index dropped by pip as untrusted

failureDiagnosis.case: pip's "is not a trusted or secure host" warning -> names SANDBOX_PIP_TRUSTED_HOST
not-found markers AND a successful probe -> points at the distribution name (often not the import name) or the mirror's contents

case.condition: pip exited 0 but the kernel cannot see the package

failureDiagnosis.case: install_status: FAILED, because pip's exit code proves a download, not an import

timeout.note: Ceiling on the background pip run. The TOOL CALL itself never blocks longer than SANDBOX_TOOL_BUDGET (45s), which must stay under the MCP client's own request timeout.

tool.name: reset_kernel_state
tool.description: Restart ONE namespace's kernel, clearing that conversation's in-memory state. Workspace files kept; other namespaces untouched.

embeddedRules.notAppliedReason: _RULES opens by demanding a namespace these tools do not take; adding ~500 tokens of kernel rules would undo the low-load design
embeddedRules.rule: No pip/apt/conda, no network. All libraries pre-installed.
matplotlib savefig+close (no show); plotly write_html; save pptx/pdf/docx/html into ./workspace.
On stderr error, fix and retry.

toolBoundaries.note: overlapping tools are how small models pick the wrong one; keep these pointers in sync with the descriptions
toolBoundaries.boundary: "To simply SAVE text or code to a file without running it, use write_workspace_file instead -- it is simpler and needs no namespace."
Appended to the response for a .py target: "Next: run it with run_python_file(...)".
